column1: # The three team modes every agent session runs with, and the skills the rules name, one
# definition for every tool.
# Columns: tool <TAB> mode <TAB> level <TAB> probe <TAB> install <TAB> verified
# The rules say no work starts until the three modes are active (rules.md, the language rules).
# This file is what holds that: session-start and start-issue run team-modes-check, which reads
# the rows for the tools found on this machine and refuses the session when a mode is missing,
# printing the install column for it. team-modes-install runs that column. The push hook runs
# the same check, so a push cannot go out of a session that never had them.
# tool     the agent tool, by the name of its command on PATH: claude, codex, gemini. A tool
#          whose command has another name gets its own rows once somebody who uses it adds them.
# mode     caveman (terse output), ponytail (the lazy senior developer's decision ladder),
#          i-have-adhd (action first, numbered, no preamble).
#          archify (interactive diagrams, the skill rules/skills.md names for documenting a structure).
# level    what the mode is set to when it is activated in a session: lite, full, on. Caveman
#          stays at lite: it shortens the chat answer, never the record and never what is read.
#          "-" is a skill the rules name that is installed and checked but not switched on at
#          session start: the tool loads it when a task calls for it (archify).
# probe    how the check sees that the mode is installed for that tool:
#            plugin:NAME  the tool's own plugin list names it (claude plugin list,
#                         codex plugin list, gemini extensions list)
#            skill:NAME   a skill folder of that name exists in the tool's skill directories or
#                         in the shared .agents/skills directory the skills installer writes
#            file:PATH    that file exists (~ is the home directory)
#            none         nobody has written a probe yet - the check REFUSES and says so, so the
#                         first person who uses the tool fills the row in rather than guessing
#            always       counts as installed; only for tests
# install  the command that installs it, run by team-modes-install; "-" where the tool's own
#          documentation is the only source (the check prints its address instead)
# verified LOGIN,DATE of the person who ran the probe and the install on that tool, or "-".
#          A row marked "-" is a reading of the mode's documentation, not a proof.
claude
claude
claude
column5: claude plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail && claude plugin install ponytail@ponytail
